title: Heat
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child lists sources of heat (sun, fire, stoves, electricity) and says what heat is used for, and how to save it.
representations: pictures of a jiko, iron, kettle, sun, gas cooker
two wet cloths for the sun test
steps: Say what each is used for.

board.do: Draw the sun, a jiko and an iron.

board.say: What do we use its heat for?

board.do: Wait for the child to say ironing clothes.
Draw a line from each source to its use.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a source of heat: a torch or a charcoal jiko?
misconceptions.repair: Hold a hand near a torch and near a warm jiko (safely). Feel which is warm.

misconceptions.ask: Why do clothes dry when hung in the sun?
misconceptions.repair: Put two wet cloths, one in sun and one in shade. Feel and compare after an hour.

listen_for: Uncovered, so we can see it
misconceptions.ask: Which pot of water boils faster: covered or uncovered?
misconceptions.repair: Boil two small pots, one covered. Time them. Say: the lid keeps heat in and saves fuel.

listen_for: Leave it, it will go out
misconceptions.ask: Cooking is finished. What should be done with the fire?
misconceptions.repair: Show how embers can flare up and burn. An adult puts out the fire; children keep away.

checks.question: Name a source of heat.
checks.answer: The sun (fire, a jiko, an iron)

checks.question: What is heat used for at home?
